name: Shatter
how_it_smokes: Clean and potent with a glassy snap; flavor is present but more muted than a badder or live product. Breaks into brittle, translucent shards and handles easily on a dab tool.
good_for: when you want a strong, clean hit and easy, room-stable handling.
notes: The glassy texture comes from minimal agitation and a longer purge, which also drives off some terpenes, so it tastes cleaner but less loud than badder or live extracts. Can slowly 'auto-budder' (turn waxy) if it warms or has residual terps.

name: Badder
how_it_smokes: Smooth and flavorful with a creamy, cake-batter texture that scoops easily. More aromatic than shatter; dab it low to keep the terps.
good_for: a flavorful, easy-to-scoop dab that loads onto a tool without the mess of sauce.
notes: Badder and budder differ mainly in whip and texture: badder is softer and more spreadable. 'Batter' is just an alternate spelling. Live versions (live badder) start from fresh-frozen and hit harder on flavor.

name: Budder
how_it_smokes: Creamy and smooth like badder but thicker and more opaque, with a frosting-like body. Flavorful; dab low to preserve the aroma.
good_for: the same flavorful, scoopable appeal as badder but a touch denser and easier to dose.
notes: Whipped/agitated further than badder during the purge, which builds that dense creamy texture. The badder/budder naming is used loosely and varies shop to shop.

name: Wax
how_it_smokes: Soft, opaque, and easy to handle, with a solid potent hit and moderate flavor. 'Wax' is a catch-all, so taste and quality vary a lot by producer.
good_for: an approachable, often cheaper dab and a common first concentrate.
notes: Older umbrella term that overlaps with budder and crumble; modern menus tend to use the more specific names. Texture ranges from soft and pliable to slightly crumbly.

name: Crumble
how_it_smokes: Dry, brittle, and crumbly, breaking apart into a honeycomb-like powder. Potent with decent flavor, and versatile because it sprinkles easily over flower.
good_for: topping a bowl or joint and simple to portion for a dab.
notes: The crumbly texture comes from a longer, lower-temperature purge. Easy to add on top of flower, though it can be messy as it falls apart.

name: Sauce
how_it_smokes: Intensely flavorful and aromatic; the wet, terpene-rich liquid carries loud taste, usually with crystalline THCA 'diamonds' suspended in it. Sticky and hard to handle; dab low to do the terps justice.
good_for: chasing maximum flavor; a favorite for flavor-focused dabbers.
notes: 'Sauce' names the texture: a high-terpene liquid that has separated out, usually with THCA diamonds sitting in it. Most prized as live resin sauce (fresh-frozen); cured versions exist but carry less aroma. Many people dab the diamonds and sauce together.

name: Sugar
how_it_smokes: Grainy and crystalline like wet sugar, with good flavor and a strong hit. Easier to scoop than sauce but still a bit sticky; dab low to keep the terps.
good_for: a flavorful dab that's a little easier to handle than runny sauce.
notes: A texture of small THCA crystals suspended in terpene liquid. Live resin sugar (fresh-frozen) is more aromatic; cured sugar is more affordable. Sits between badder and sauce in handling.

name: THCA Diamonds
how_it_smokes: Extremely potent but, on their own, fairly flavorless; the crystalline THCA carries the strength while the surrounding sauce carries the taste. Most people dab diamonds and sauce together. Clear, crystal-like chunks that handle easily.
good_for: maximum potency, usually dabbed together with the sauce for flavor.
notes: Nearly pure THCA crystalline (often 95%+). Grown ('mined') from a high-terpene extract; the terps separate into the sauce, so a clean diamond is potent but not flavorful by itself. THCA converts to THC when heated.

name: Live Resin
how_it_smokes: Loud, true-to-strain flavor and a smooth, well-rounded high. Made from fresh-frozen plants, so it keeps the volatile terpenes that curing would lose; presents in textures from sauce to badder to sugar.
good_for: flavor and a fuller, more complete high while still being scoopable.
notes: 'Live' means the plant was frozen fresh at harvest instead of dried and cured, preserving terpenes. Still solvent-extracted (usually butane); the solventless counterpart is live rosin. The single 'consistency' here is nominal, since texture varies by producer.

name: Live Rosin
how_it_smokes: Exceptionally flavorful and smooth with a full, rounded high and no residual solvents. Pressed from fresh-frozen bubble hash, so it keeps the strain's complete terpene profile.
good_for: the top-shelf, no-solvent choice for purists, usually at a premium price.
notes: Solventless: fresh-frozen flower to bubble hash to a heat-and-pressure press. The connoisseur's concentrate. 'Live rosin' (fresh-frozen) sits a step above standard rosin (cured input). The premium price reflects the labor and low yield.

name: Rosin
how_it_smokes: Clean, solventless, and flavorful, though a notch below live rosin since it starts from cured material. Pressed with just heat and pressure; texture ranges from sappy to badder.
good_for: a solventless dab without the live-rosin price tag, and simple enough to press at home.
notes: Heat plus pressure, no solvents. Made from cured flower (flower rosin) or cured bubble hash (hash rosin); hash rosin is higher quality. 'Live rosin' specifically means fresh-frozen input. DIY-friendly with a press.

name: Distillate
how_it_smokes: Very high THC but essentially flavorless on its own, since distillation strips the terpenes; producers usually re-introduce terps for taste. Thin and runny when warm, and the backbone of most vape cartridges and edibles.
good_for: high-THC potency for carts, edibles, and infusing, where consistency matters more than flavor.
notes: Refined by distillation to isolate cannabinoids, removing terpenes and most everything else. Potent but one-note without added terps, and lacks the full-spectrum effect of live products.

name: RSO (Rick Simpson Oil)
how_it_smokes: Primarily an ingestible oil, not a dab: thick, dark, and bitter, taken orally in tiny doses. It can be dabbed but burns harsh and isn't made for flavor. Whole-plant and decarboxylated, so it's active when eaten.
temp_range_f: n/a - usually taken orally, not dabbed
good_for: medicinal, high-dose full-spectrum use; usually a rice-grain oral dose rather than a dab.
notes: A whole-plant extract made with ethanol or similar and reduced to a thick, decarbed oil. Associated with high-dose medicinal use. Valued for breadth of cannabinoids, not flavor or dabbing.

name: Bubble Hash
how_it_smokes: Solventless and flavorful, ranging from sandy lower grades (best sprinkled on a bowl) to 'full-melt' that bubbles and vaporizes cleanly enough to dab. Made by agitating trichomes off the plant in ice water and sieving them by size.
good_for: a solventless option; top grades can be dabbed, lower grades go on flower.
notes: Graded 1-6 stars by how cleanly it melts; only full-melt (5-6 star) dabs well. Fresh-frozen bubble hash is the starting point for live rosin. Quality depends on keeping trichome heads intact, so retention varies by grade.

name: Traditional Hash
how_it_smokes: The classic pressed-resin smoke: earthy, aromatic, and milder than modern concentrates. Usually crumbled into a joint or smoked in a pipe rather than dabbed. Texture runs from pliable to hard depending on origin and age.
good_for: an old-world smoke to add to a joint or bowl; widely available and approachable.
notes: Made by mechanically collecting and pressing trichomes (dry-sift kief) or hand-rubbing fresh plants (charas). Long history across Morocco, Afghanistan, Lebanon, India and beyond. Less potent than BHO or rosin but prized for tradition.

name: Kief
how_it_smokes: The loose, sandy trichome powder that sifts off flower: more potent than bud and simple to sprinkle on a bowl or twist into a joint. Mild, flowery flavor; usually smoked with flower rather than dabbed.
temp_range_f: n/a - usually smoked with flower, not dabbed
good_for: an easy potency boost on a bowl or in a joint; can also be pressed into rosin.
notes: Just the dry-sifted resin glands (trichomes). The kief catch in a three-chamber grinder collects it over time. Press it with heat to make rosin, or pile it on a bowl for a boost.

name: Sap (Pull-and-Snap)
how_it_smokes: A pliable, taffy-like consistency that 'pulls and snaps', sitting between glassy shatter and creamy badder. Slightly more flavorful than shatter thanks to a touch more terpene content, and easier to portion without shattering.
good_for: a middle-ground BHO that's easier to handle than brittle shatter.
notes: Sometimes just called 'sap.' No exact 'sap' texture token exists in the controlled set, so it is filed under the shatter family it comes from. The taffy feel comes from a bit more residual terpenes/moisture than stable shatter; can sugar up toward budder over time.

name: CO2 Oil
how_it_smokes: Smooth and runny, and common in vape cartridges. Flavor varies a lot: supercritical CO2 can keep some terpenes, but many products strip and re-add them. Potent but usually not as flavorful as live solventless options.
good_for: vape cartridges and a cleaner-feeling extraction; potency and flavor depend on whether terps are reintroduced.
notes: Extracted with pressurized CO2. Often marketed as 'clean' or even mislabeled 'solventless' - CO2 is a solvent, just one that leaves no residual taste. Terpenes are frequently separated and reintroduced.
